text:
kai: Heads-up — after the kernel-selection RFC landed I ran quick perf passes toggling FlashAttention v2 vs v3 on dev cluster. Seeing regressions for long-context + KV-cache heavy runs (seq=4096). Sharing numbers and questions.

maya: thanks — do you have the exact bench command and hardware? might be shape/workspace related.

kai: bench command I used: ```python bench.py --model gpt-neox-20b --seq 4096 --batch 1 --kernels flashattn_v2,flashattn_v3 --dtype fp16 --device a100-sxm-80gb --kv-cache true --warmups 10 --steps 100``` 

todd: nice, can you paste the raw numbers from the run?

kai: infra bot posted the CI summary but raw: v2: 112 tok/s, v3: 98 tok/s (single-stream generation). Mem high-water: v2 43.6GB, v3 40.2GB. So v3 reduced peak mem ~8% but throughput down ~12.5% for this shape.

infra-bot: Perf job 1744012350 completed — details: a100-sxm-80gb, fp16, gpt-neox-20b, seq=4096, batch=1. flashattn_v2: 112 tok/s, flashattn_v3: 98 tok/s, peak_mem_v2=43.6GB, peak_mem_v3=40.2GB, mean_latency_v2=210ms, mean_latency_v3=240ms.

maya: sounds like v3 changed workspace tradeoffs. v3 often reduces temporary allocations by streaming/blocking but adds extra kernel launches for certain head/group shapes. On long seq it can thrash kernel launch overhead.

samir: is there a difference if you force group_size or head_dim alignment? v3 sometimes benefits when head_dim % 64 == 0.

kai: tried head_dim align to 64 and reran: v2 118 tok/s, v3 120 tok/s for head_dim=64 case. So alignment matters a lot. Seems our kernel selector missed selecting v3 only when shape was favorable.

todd: that's interesting — maybe our selector heuristics prefer v2 for seq>2048 by default. We should expose a per-model override or a perf probe that records shape-level perf and updates the policy.

eva: also worth checking CUDA kernel workspace size limits. v3 may require larger workspace buffers that we currently allocate from a pooled allocator with small-chunk eviction which increases fragmentation and lead to extra cudaMallocSyncs.

maya: if fragmentation is the culprit, we could reserve a contiguous workspace for attention kernels before running generation instead of relying on on-demand pools. That would trade memory for stability.

samir: what about quantized paths? flashattn_v3 with q4 ops — any numbers?

kai: quick q4hx run: v2(q4): 160 tok/s, v3(q4): 152 tok/s. smaller delta but still favors v2 on that shape. Also saw occasional kernel fallback warnings in logs: "FlashAttentionV3: workspace too small, falling back to v2 kernel" — need to capture that in traces.

todd: action items: 1) add perf probe to kernel selector that records per (model,seq,batch,head_dim) performance, 2) detect and log workspace fallback events centrally, 3) experiment with preallocated attention workspace for long contexts.

maya: +1. I'll prototype a small allocator switcher that preallocs for attention kernels and exposes env var REDWOOD_ATTENTION_PREALLOC=true for testing.

infra-bot: CI perf-run queued: 1744013000 will run v2/v3 across shapes: seq=512,1024,2048,4096; head_dim variants 64/80/96; batches 1/2. Expect results in ~45m.

kai: thanks — we'll regroup after CI. Also note for RFC follow-up: we should update kernel-selection RFC with explicit shape heuristics and a fallback telemetry section so platform can auto-tune customer workloads.

eva: FYI — Triton-backed flash kernels show smaller launch overhead when compiled for our CUDA arch. Could be another angle if v3 CPU-side launches are the bottleneck.

todd: great thread. tagging @oncall-eng-runtime to keep an eye on perf regressions in staging.

samir: one more ask: include synthetic peak mem + p99 latency charts in the perf probes so we can balance mem vs throughput automatically.

kai: noted. I'll file a short follow-up RFC PR with proposed selector changes and test plan after CI completes. :rocket:
